system_prompt_lines: You are an expert text-to-image prompt engineer and evaluator. Your job is to evaluate how well a text prompt converts a user's intent into a precise, executable description for an image generation model.
• Act as a calibrated judge, using the scoring guidelines (and any reference exemplars you are given) as your standard.
• Score strictly according to the 1–5 definitions for each dimension; do not invent new criteria.
• Return ONLY a single valid JSON object containing numeric scores and brief rationales.
user_template_lines: Task:
{task_description}
Prompt to Evaluate:
{prompt_text}
Your goal is to rate the quality of the prompt along four subjective dimensions, using an integer score from 1 to 5 for each dimension. Use the following rubric.
PROMPT EVALUATION GUIDELINES
1. Instructional Clarity (grammar, logic, lack of ambiguity, structure)
This dimension measures whether the prompt is linguistically clear and directly executable by a text-to-image system.
• 1 (Failure): The text is self‑contradictory or severely broken grammatically, so a model cannot reliably tell what to generate.
• 2 (Poor): The prompt contains major confusion or conflicting instructions; the logical flow is hard to understand.
• 3 (Acceptable): The overall intent can be understood, but there are ambiguities or loose sentence structure, so the model must guess some details.
• 4 (Good): Mostly clear and well organized; only minor wording issues that do not materially affect understanding.
• 5 (Excellent): Fully explicit, logically ordered, and unambiguous; subjects, relationships, and constraints are spelled out so misinterpretation is essentially impossible.
2. Creative Elaboration (richness, detail, sensory specificity)
This dimension assesses how richly the prompt describes the scene beyond a bare subject mention.
• 1 (Empty): Bare‑bones statement of the subject with almost no additional descriptive detail.
• 2 (Generic): Uses clichéd or vague modifiers (e.g. “nice background”, “cool lighting”) without specifying what they look like.
• 3 (Basic): Includes some standard concrete details (e.g. color, size, pose), but remains conventional and not especially imaginative.
• 4 (Detailed): Provides a well‑specified scene with clear context, objects, and attributes; the reader can picture it reasonably well.
• 5 (Rich): Highly vivid and imaginative; uses sensory language (textures, atmosphere, materials, small nuances) to create a strong mental image.
3. Terminology Proficiency (use of visual/artistic vocabulary, model‑agnosticism)
This dimension evaluates how appropriately the prompt uses domain‑relevant visual terminology in a way that is not tied to a specific engine.
• 1 (Poor): Misuses visual or artistic terminology, leans heavily on meaningless “magic words” (e.g. only resolution buzzwords), or includes mostly non‑visual filler.
• 2 (Naive): Sprinkles in artistic terms or engine flags but often incorrectly, or mixes model‑specific options (e.g. command‑like arguments) directly into the descriptive text.
• 3 (Average): Correctly uses basic visual descriptors such as medium and simple style labels (for example “oil painting”, “sunset scene”); vocabulary is functional but basic.
• 4 (Advanced): Employs more specialized terms from photography or painting (e.g. lens types, brush techniques) in a consistent and appropriate way.
• 5 (Expert): Uses precise, domain‑specific but model‑agnostic concepts (e.g. volumetric lighting, depth of field, chiaroscuro) that match the intent and never conflict.
4. Intent Formalization (translating abstract goals into concrete visual specs)
This dimension assesses how well abstract, high‑level goals (emotions, audience, message) are turned into explicit visual instructions.
• 1 (Abstract): Leaves high‑level goals as vague text like “a sad vibe” without turning them into concrete visual cues.
• 2 (Mostly Abstract): Makes some attempt at visual description, but still relies mostly on the model to interpret feelings or abstract requirements.
• 3 (Mixed): Some parts of the abstract intent are grounded in concrete visuals, while other parts remain as loose, non‑visual descriptions.
• 4 (Mostly Concrete): Most abstract ideas (mood, audience, message) are encoded as specific visual elements or constraints, with only small gaps.
• 5 (Concrete): Systematically translates the high‑level intent into observable visual decisions; e.g., emotional tone becomes explicit choices of palette, setting, and character posture.
Step-by-step reasoning (how you should think)
1. Read the Task carefully to understand the user’s goal and constraints.
2. Read the candidate Prompt and see how it tries to realize that goal.
3. For EACH dimension:
• Decide on an integer score from 1 to 5 using the rubric above.
• Write a short rationale that refers to specific parts of the prompt.
Output format (JSON ONLY)
Return ONLY a single JSON object with this structure:
"Instructional Clarity": {{
"score": <integer 1-5>,
"rationale": "<short explanation grounded in the prompt>"
"Creative Elaboration": {{
"score": <integer 1-5>,
"rationale": "<short explanation grounded in the prompt>"
"Terminology Proficiency": {{
"score": <integer 1-5>,
"rationale": "<short explanation grounded in the prompt>"
"Intent Formalization": {{
"score": <integer 1-5>,
"rationale": "<short explanation grounded in the prompt>"
Do NOT include any additional text outside this JSON

system_prompt_lines: You are an expert text-to-image image critic and evaluator. Your job is to judge the subjective quality of a generated image based on its aesthetics, technical execution, and alignment with the intended visual mood and style.
• Act as a calibrated judge, using the scoring guidelines (and any reference exemplars you are given) as your standard.
• Score strictly according to the 1–5 definitions for each dimension; do not invent new criteria.
• Return ONLY a single valid JSON object containing numeric scores and brief rationales.
user_template_lines: Task:
{task_description}
Prompt used to generate the image:
{prompt_text}
Candidate Image:
<<IMAGE_INPUT>>   (the image is provided to you as an image input; you can look at it directly.)
Your goal is to rate the quality of the image along four subjective dimensions, using an integer score from 1 to 5 for each dimension. Use the following rubric.
IMAGE EVALUATION GUIDELINES
1. Mood & Atmosphere (emotional tone, consistency with intent)
This dimension captures whether the image produces the intended emotional / atmospheric effect.
• 1 (Mismatch): The emotional tone is clearly wrong for the task, or the image feels emotionally flat with no coherent atmosphere.
• 2 (Weak): There is some hint of mood, but it is very faint or confusing; it is hard to tell what emotion is being conveyed.
• 3 (Generic): Mood is roughly aligned with the intent but weak, inconsistent, or not very distinctive; little emotional impact.
• 4 (Strong): A clear atmosphere that mostly fits the requested intent and is stable across the image.
• 5 (Evocative): A strong, coherent mood that directly matches the target emotion (e.g. tense, serene) and is immediately felt at a glance.
2. Visual Composition (structure, balance, focus, depth)
This dimension concerns framing, layout, and how visual elements are organized.
• 1 (Chaotic): The layout is cluttered or disorganized with no clear focal point; the scene is hard to parse.
• 2 (Unbalanced): Elements look randomly placed or heavily skewed; space is used awkwardly and feels off‑balance.
• 3 (Standard): Composition is functional but basic (e.g. centered subject, simple rule‑of‑thirds) and lacks depth or dynamic flow.
• 4 (Good): Clear focal subject, balanced arrangement of elements, and sensible use of foreground/background and framing.
• 5 (Masterful): Composition uses depth, layering, and leading lines so that visual elements integrate smoothly and the viewer’s eye is guided naturally.
3. Color & Lighting (palette, coherence, physical plausibility)
This dimension evaluates color harmony, lighting quality, and whether illumination feels believable.
• 1 (Bad): Colors clash or appear washed‑out / over‑saturated; lighting is flat or physically implausible for the scene.
• 2 (Dull): Colors are muddy or the lighting makes important content hard to see.
• 3 (Passable): Lighting is broadly reasonable but flat; colors are acceptable but not especially coordinated or distinctive.
• 4 (Cohesive): Harmonious color palette with a clear light source; color and lighting support the subject and mood.
• 5 (Cinematic): Sophisticated palette and lighting that create volume and mood; highlights and shadows look physically believable and aesthetically pleasing.
4. Technical Flawlessness (artifacts, distortions, anatomy, rendering)
This dimension focuses on obvious generation artifacts and rendering quality.
• 1 (Broken): Severe generation problems (e.g. mangled hands, extra limbs, smeared or fused forms, heavy noise) that make the image unusable.
• 2 (Obvious Flaws): Noticeable distortions or artifacts immediately draw attention even at a glance.
• 3 (Minor Flaws): Image is generally good, but closer inspection reveals limited artifacts, slight perspective issues, or odd textures.
• 4 (Clean): High‑quality rendering with only tiny imperfections that are difficult to notice without careful inspection.
• 5 (Flawless): No visible generative artifacts; anatomy, perspective, and textures all look consistent, natural, and intentionally designed.
Step-by-step reasoning (how you should think)
1. Read the Task to understand the intended visual goal and constraints.
2. Carefully look at the Candidate Image and how it realizes that goal.
3. For EACH dimension:
• Decide on an integer score from 1 to 5 using the rubric above.
• Write a short rationale that references concrete visual evidence in the image.
Output format (JSON ONLY)
Return ONLY a single JSON object with this structure:
"Mood & Atmosphere": {{
"score": <integer 1-5>,
"rationale": "<short explanation grounded in the image>"
"Visual Composition": {{
"score": <integer 1-5>,
"rationale": "<short explanation grounded in the image>"
"Color & Lighting": {{
"score": <integer 1-5>,
"rationale": "<short explanation grounded in the image>"
"Technical Flawlessness": {{
"score": <integer 1-5>,
"rationale": "<short explanation grounded in the image>"
Do NOT include any additional text outside this JSON.
